title: PAL and NTSC player-menu sizing
symptom: The NTSC CD-i 220 player menu appears vertically larger or more stretched than the PAL player menu when each is presented at 4:3.
expected: Each player ROM uses its hardware-correct 525/60 or 625/50 raster and pixel aspect; any remaining layout difference is attributable to the corresponding BIOS artwork rather than frontend distortion.

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The 525-line presentation path may apply an incorrect vertical scale or aperture relative to the 625-line path.
supporting_evidence: Side-by-side 4:3 screenshots make the NTSC menu artwork appear taller and more vertically crowded.
contradicting_evidence: The screenshots come from different PAL and NTSC player firmware, which may intentionally lay out the shell differently.
No real-hardware capture or common source asset has yet established the expected relative dimensions.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Capture the live MCD212 timing and aperture for both ROMs, verify frontend pixel-aspect math from the specifications, and compare against real-hardware captures or measurements of a common geometric element.
citations: Green Book V.2.2, V.2.3, and V.4.8

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The PAL and NTSC player ROMs intentionally use different coordinates or artwork proportions for their different active-line counts.
supporting_evidence: The Philips logo, background-disc spacing, controls, and pointer placement differ together rather than looking like a uniform scale of one identical image.
contradicting_evidence: A frontend scaling error could still exaggerate an intentional layout difference.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Compare raw composed rasters before frontend scaling and inspect the firmware's MCD212/DCA positioning for corresponding menu elements.

manual_verification.notes: User supplied PAL and NTSC player-menu screenshots and explicitly marked the possible NTSC stretching as uncertain.
